paper_title: MARBLE A Hard Benchmark for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning and Planning
caption: : Search space of the dataset under different configurations.
model_annotation: The plot titled “Search Space of M-Cube” illustrates how the number of possible solutions changes as the number of missing pieces increases, under two configurations shown in the legend (“Flip needed” and “Flip ignored”). The x-axis is labeled “# Missing pieces,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 1 to 6 with ticks at every 1. The y-axis is labeled “# Possible solutions,” uses a logarithmic (base-10) scale, and shows major tick labels at \(10^2\), \(10^4\), \(10^6\), and \(10^8\) (with values extending from below \(10^2\) up to around \(10^8\)). The “Flip needed” series is drawn as a solid orange line with circular markers and increases steadily across the x-axis, starting below \(10^2\) at 1 missing piece, reaching about \(10^2\) at 2 missing pieces, rising to between \(10^4\) and \(10^6\) around 4 missing pieces, and ending near \(10^8\) at 6 missing pieces. The “Flip ignored” series is drawn as a solid light-blue line with circular markers and also increases monotonically, starting below \(10^2\) at 1 missing piece, remaining below the orange series at each x-value, reaching around \(10^4\) by 4 missing pieces, and ending between \(10^6\) and \(10^8\) (closer to \(10^6\)) at 6 missing pieces; two red text annotations label “CUBE-easy” near the point around x=2 and “CUBE” near the point at x=6 on the upper (orange) curve.
